summary: Flake 2 is much thinner than flake 1 (E2g area ~10x smaller, same power/time/514.5 nm), and its E2g band is blue-shifted by 2.8 ± 0.3 cm-1 (1368.99 vs 1366.19) and ~20% broader. This is compatible with a monolayer or few-layer hBN, but Raman alone cannot establish it is a monolayer. Flake 1's thickness is unknown, and its width (~16-19 cm-1) is already abnormal for bulk hBN. AFM or the low-frequency shear mode is needed to settle the layer number.

observations.finding: Flake 2 gives a much weaker E2g signal than flake 1, so it is much thinner; layer count not determined
observations.evidence: E2g area 73,000 (flake 1) vs 7,300 (flake 2) counts*cm-1, ratio ~10; height ~3200 vs ~270-290 counts above baseline; S/N ~80 vs ~14. If flake 1 were N layers, flake 2 would be ~N/10; N unknown.

observations.finding: E2g of flake 2 is blue-shifted and broader than that of flake 1
observations.evidence: Lorentzian fit 1366.19 ± 0.04 vs 1368.99 ± 0.23 cm-1 (centroids 1366.3 vs 1368.7); FWHM 18.0 ± 0.1 vs 21.6 ± 0.8 (Lorentz), 19.2 vs 23.8 (Voigt), 15.7 vs 18.0 direct half-max

observations.finding: Flake 1 is unexpectedly broad for bulk hBN, so it is a poor bulk reference; part of the flake 2 shift/broadening could be disorder or strain
observations.evidence: Flake 1 FWHM ~16-19 cm-1 vs ~8-9 cm-1 recalled for good bulk crystals; Si 520 FWHM 3.75-3.87 cm-1 so instrument resolution is not the cause
observations.source: Nemanich et al., PRB 23, 6348 (1981) for bulk linewidth (from memory)

observations.finding: Si 520 signal is ~18x stronger on flake 2, consistent with flake 1 perturbing the optical path much more (thicker) than flake 2
observations.evidence: Si 520 height ~930 (flake 1) vs ~17,000 (flake 2) counts; Si position 520.92/520.90 cm-1 identical, FWHM 3.75/3.87; Si 2TO near 950 cm-1 visible only on flake 2. hBN is transparent at 514.5 nm so this is interference/scattering/focus, not absorption.

observations.finding: Low optical contrast of flake 2 is expected for monolayer to few-layer hBN on 290 nm SiO2 and does not discriminate layer number
observations.evidence: Qualitative: researcher reports flake 2 barely visible; monolayer contrast only a few percent

observations.finding: A blue shift of the hBN E2g band toward thin layers has been reported but the magnitude is small and disputed, and comparable to strain/substrate effects
observations.evidence: Observed +2.8 ± 0.3 cm-1, similar in size to the reported monolayer-vs-bulk shift of ~+2 cm-1
observations.source: Gorbachev et al., Small 7, 465 (2011); Cai et al. on few-layer hBN Raman and phonon dispersion (recalled from memory, figure numbers not verified)

properties.name: layers
properties.value: thinner than flake 1; consistent with 1 layer but not established (1 to a few layers cannot be separated); flake 1 thickness unknown

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: not determined; flake 1 E2g unusually broad (~16-19 cm-1), possibly disorder or turbostratic stacking

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: not determined (blue shift of +2.8 cm-1 could be thinness, compressive strain or doping)

caveats: Intensity ratio of ~10 assumes identical focus, polarisation, objective and substrate; focus alone could change it by a factor of 2 or more, and it gives no layer count without flake 1's thickness.
Si 520 intensity differs by ~18x between flakes through SiO2 interference and focus; normalising E2g to Si is unreliable.
Shift and width differences are only a few times the fit uncertainty; the literature layer-dependent shift is small and overlaps with strain, substrate and doping effects.
Flake 1 is itself broad (low crystal quality or turbostratic), so flake 1 to flake 2 is not a clean bulk to monolayer comparison.
The measured range (450-1650 cm-1) excludes the ~50 cm-1 low-frequency shear mode, which would show whether flake 2 has more than one layer.
FWHM depends on line shape and baseline choice; the spread in flake 2 widths (18-24 cm-1) is larger than the quoted fit error.
Single spot per flake: uniformity, folds and thickness steps are not probed.
questions_for_user: Can you take AFM of flake 2? A step height of ~0.4-1 nm versus >1 nm is the decisive test for a monolayer.
Is there a known 1L or 2L flake from the same batch to calibrate intensity and shift?
Can you measure the low-frequency range (<100 cm-1) for the shear mode? Its absence would favour a monolayer.
Were focus, polarisation, grating and objective identical for both flakes, and were the E2g peaks unsaturated?
What is flake 1's thickness (AFM or contrast) and what is the hBN source (HPHT, CVD, commercial)? Its broad line needs explaining.
Can you map E2g intensity and position across flake 2 to check uniformity?
citations: Gorbachev et al., Small 7, 465 (2011), 'Hunting for monolayer boron nitride: optical and Raman signatures' (recalled from memory; figure numbers not checked)
Nemanich, Solin, Guerard, Phys. Rev. B 23, 6348 (1981), Raman of hexagonal BN (recalled from memory; bulk E2g ~1366 cm-1, linewidth)
Cai et al., Raman signature and phonon dispersion of few-layer hBN (recalled from memory; figure numbers not checked)
limits: The E2g intensity scales with layer number but there is no calibration on these two spectra.
Raman here gives a thickness ranking, not an absolute layer count.
Cannot separate strain, doping and disorder contributions to the shift and width.
Cannot establish stacking order or lateral uniformity from two single-spot spectra.
Cannot be quantitative about the layer-dependent shift because the literature values are quoted from memory and are disputed.
